scope: Three open items from capacity-real-send: (1) per-stage breakdown of chat delivery from socket frame receipt, one targeted reversible change, re-measured; (2) the stalled-Redis lease that kept renewing; (3) the soak's publish denials and call-status errors. Local only, no cloud.

method.frameDiagnostics: test-support/native-rds-preload.mjs ORGIQ_NATIVE_METRICS_MODE=frames (bind-mounted; bff-cluster-containers.py ORGIQ_BFF_CONTAINER_METRICS_MODE=frames). Hooks: ws 'message' receipt per connection, createWsHandler services' handleAction (queue wait = handler start - receipt; blockedBy = overlap with earlier handlers on the same connection), chat send gates/persist/broadcast, Redis router publish/receive, recipient socket write, outgoing error frames by fixed labels, host membership writes/peer hints/fences, SQL and Dynamo error classes. log2/8 histograms (~9% resolution; percentiles report the bucket upper bound). SIGUSR2 resets after fixture preparation. Counts/timings only; no channels, subjects, ids or bodies written. Wall-clock spans across containers use the one VM kernel clock.

item1_breakdown.burst: burst-frames-1 (driver p50 2,702): send.queueWait p50 663-723 / p95 1,116-1,327 ms (blocked by the same socket's presence.set in 410/620 sends, overlap p50 ~750 ms); handler start->message created p50 139-255 / p95 469-608 (publish authorize p50 ~100, p95 430); created->peer recipient write p50 1,721 / p95 1,877-2,232 (created->peer publish p50 0.86-1.1 s = persist ~0.21 + publish check ~0.1 + local fan-out ~0.15-0.2 + second check; Redis transit ~0.1-0.16; peer receive->write ~0.86 incl. publisher+recipient authorize); event-loop delay p50 10.2 (resolution floor) / p99 40 / max 167-214 ms; frame parse+dispatch for an unblocked frame <=0.1 ms p50 (max 3 ms); socket send backlog 0 KB at every write. Server sum of p50s ~2.61 s vs driver 2.70 s; ~0.09 s outside the server. burst-frames-2 (driver p50 4.70 s): queue p50 2.43 s (send enqueued behind join/subscribe/set).
item1_breakdown.soak: soak-frames-1/before-3: send.queueWait p50 0.1 / p95 2.9-3.2 s / p99 4.1-4.9 s, blocked by presence.set (~45% of sends, overlap p50 938 ms) and earlier chat.send; presence.set handler p50 860 ms (permitted 394, broadcast 663-789, shared store put 24 ms); chat.send handler p50 37 / p95 2,047. soak-frames-2 diverged (driver p95 12.2 s; presence.set queue p95 16-19 s as the driver's 1-s recovery retries stack per socket).
item1_breakdown.rootMechanism: Every slow stage is authorization I/O under a saturated fixture: BFF containers reach their 1-CPU cap during waves, DynamoDB Local 86% of a core, ~1.3 ms CPU per SDK call; authorize allow p50 ~100 ms / p95 360-720 ms. Earlier SDK pool experiment (128) did not help; this stage did not repeat it.

soak.verdict: Lane soaks are below every baseline soak and none diverged (baseline diverged in 2 of 6), but the non-divergent baselines (3.1-4.2 s) overlap closely. Queue wait halves; work moves into handler time because the CPU is saturated. Capacity still fails (300 ms target).

item2_redisStall.finding: Not a fenced owner and not the fixture client. Each BFF has two leased routers: /ws (namespace) and cookie /realtime (namespace:distillation). During the 12-s pause both routers' renewals were in flight; the cookie router's 2-s command deadline fired ~60 ms before the paused EVAL replies were delivered, so it fenced (health 503), while the /ws router's reply landed inside its deadline and it legitimately kept its lease, renewing every 10 s from the same connection with its own token (stall-repro-1-monitor.txt/keys.txt). The fixture's key pattern matches both namespaces. Fenced routers never renewed. Race-dependent: 1 of 4 reproductions hit it.
item2_redisStall.defect: BFF: one process reported 503 forever while half its ownership stayed alive and kept serving its /ws sockets.
item2_redisStall.fix: middleware/src/lib/realtime-node-ownership.ts linkNodeOwnership: the first leased router to fence retires its sibling (shutdown releases the lease). Wired in index.ts; handles expose ownership. Regression: src/lib/__tests__/realtime-node-ownership.test.ts (4). stall-fixed-2 shows the RELEASE EVALs for both /ws leases 50 ms after the late renewals; stall-fixed-3/4 fenced naturally; 3/3 pass.

item3_classification.earlier: capacity-real-send soak: 95 AUTHZ_CHANNEL_DENIED (publish on the sender's own social:dm pair; samples show both members of a pair) + 6 call status refusals; soak-ab-before-1 here: 13 call status refusals, 0 denials.
item3_classification.reproduction: 0 denials and 0 protocol errors in 5 further baseline soaks (3 instrumented, 2 plain with host refusal logs) and 3 lane soaks. Both occurrences were divergent runs (driver chat p95 6.4 s and 13.9 s); one other divergent run (12.2 s) had none.
item3_classification.ruledOut: membership writes, peer invalidation hints and fenced proofs: 0 in every instrumented run (the DM index never writes members); DM name guard admits both pair members; policy is static; frames on closed sockets are never delivered; peer-side publisher checks are silent.
item3_classification.classification: By elimination both families are the host authorize returning false from its catch (fail-closed on a transient exception) under overload: live-principal catches any SQL, DynamoDB SDK (2 s connect / 5 s request deadlines) or store error and denies. That is correct fail-closed behaviour; the user-visible refusal is a capacity defect, not an authority defect. The exact exception was not captured (those runs' container logs were replaced).
item3_classification.alsoSeen: ~800 silent 'refused subscribe ... user ?' per node per soak: fan-out to sockets the driver dropped during token renewal (null context) - correct, not counted by the driver.
item3_classification.nowCaptured: run_profile.sh saves host refusal lines (*-refusals.log); frames mode counts error frames, SQL/Dynamo errors and membership fences.
